User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the NEU Library Visitor App, storing their profile information and access rights.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity, corresponding to the Firebase Authentication UID.

email.description: The user's email address, strictly enforced to end with '@neu.edu.ph'.

role.description: The role of the user within the application, determining their access level. Possible values are 'admin', 'staff', or 'user' (default 'user').

college.description: The academic college or school the user belongs to. This field is nullable (can be null) until selected during the onboarding process.

isBlocked.description: A flag indicating whether the user's access to the application is currently blocked by an administrator (default false).

Visit.title: Visit
Visit.description: Records an instance of a user's visit to the NEU Library, including the timestamp and reason for the visit.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Visit entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who made the visit. (Relationship: User 1:N Visit)

timestamp.description: The date and time when the visit was recorded, typically a Firestore server timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

reason.description: The specific purpose or reason for the user's library visit, selected from predefined options.

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles. The document ID is the Firebase Authentication UID. Contains user details such as email, role, college, and 'isBlocked' status. Includes fields critical for client-side routing and display. Owners can read/update their own 'college' field. Admin users can update any 'isBlocked' or 'role' field.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user, matching the Firebase Authentication UID.

definition.description: Records individual library visits. Each document includes 'userId' (denormalized from the User entity for authorization independence and efficient querying), 'timestamp', and 'reason'. Allows users to write their own visits. Users can read/list their own visits based on 'userId'. Admin and Staff users have global read/list access to all visits.

params.name: visitId
params.description: The unique identifier for the visit record.

definition.description: A dedicated collection for robust, authorization-independent administration role checks. The existence of a document with a user's UID in this collection grants 'admin' privileges in security rules. No actual data is stored within the documents; their mere existence serves as an authorization flag.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who holds the 'admin' role, matching their Firebase Authentication UID.

definition.description: A dedicated collection for robust, authorization-independent staff role checks. The existence of a document with a user's UID in this collection grants 'staff' privileges in security rules. No actual data is stored within the documents; their mere existence serves as an authorization flag.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who holds the 'staff' role, matching their Firebase Authentication UID.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure is designed to adhere strictly to the core principles of Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and effective Access Modeling, ensuring a secure, scalable, and debuggable system. 

**Authorization Independence:**
1.  **For `visits`:** Each `visits/{visitId}` document explicitly includes a `userId` field. This denormalization is critical for Authorization Independence. It allows security rules to verify the ownership of a visit (e.g., `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId`) directly on the `Visit` document itself, without requiring any `get()` operations to retrieve the associated `User` document. This not only simplifies security rules but also makes transactions and batch writes more robust and easier to debug, as each operation can be evaluated atomically.
2.  **For Roles:** Instead of relying on the `role` field within the `users/{userId}` document for authorization in security rules, two dedicated, top-level collections are introduced: `/roles_admin/{userId}` and `/roles_staff/{userId}`. The mere *existence* of a document with the authenticated user's `uid` in these collections grants the respective administrative or staff privileges. This design completely decouples role-based authorization from the main `users` collection, enabling `exists()` checks in security rules. This eliminates `get()` calls to the `users` collection for role validation, ensuring Authorization Independence for global permission checks. The `role` field on the `users/{userId}` document will remain the source of truth for client-side routing and display, with a Cloud Function likely used to synchronize the creation/deletion of documents in the role collections based on updates to a user's `role`.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
1.  **User-Specific Data:** The `/users/{userId}` path intrinsically ensures QAPs for individual users accessing their own profile, as the `{userId}` wildcard must match `request.auth.uid`. For `visits`, the `userId` field within each `visits/{visitId}` document allows for secure and efficient user-specific `list` queries. A user can query their own visits using `db.collection('visits').where('userId', '==', request.auth.uid)`, and security rules can validate this condition with `allow list: if request.auth.uid == request.query.userId;`. This ensures that `list` operations return only data the user is authorized to see, preventing rule failures due to filtering.
2.  **Global Data for Admin/Staff:** The decision to keep `visits` as a top-level collection (`/visits/{visitId}`) is paramount for supporting the global statistics and aggregated views required by the Admin and Staff dashboards. This structure enables efficient collection-wide queries (e.g., for 'Total Visitors Today', 'This Week', 'This Month') without relying on costly and complex collection group queries. Security for these global `list` operations is enforced by checking the `request.auth.uid` against the dedicated `/roles_admin` or `/roles_staff` collections via `exists()` checks, ensuring only authorized personnel can access the aggregated data.
